text:
The Kings arrived in Washington winless in their last six games (0-4-2) and found themselves two goals down after 18 minutes. They ended the night 5-2 winners, having snapped that run with a comeback built in the final 85 seconds of the first period. Adrian Kempe cut the deficit at 19:27 and Artemi Panarin tied it at 19:58 on a shot the data gave a 2% chance of going in. Kempe added a third-period goal for two on the night, and Erik Gustafsson and Scott Laughton also scored.

The Capitals had far more of the game than the score suggests. They attempted 69 shots to 41 and led in expected goals, a measure of shot quality, 4.21 to 2.91. By the model's replays of every shot, WSH deserved to win 70 percent of the time. They outchanced LAK 1.77 to 0.81 in the third period, but the Kings scored on three of their first four looks there. Darcy Kuemper was the reason it held: he stopped 30 of 32 shots and saved 2.21 goals more than the chances against him should have allowed. Logan Thompson, by comparison, gave up four goals on 25 shots, 1.14 more than expected.

Ryan Leonard and Cole Hutson (on the power play) gave WSH its early lead, and the Capitals went 1 for 4 with the man advantage against LAK's 1 for 2. For the Kings, the win ends a six-game winless stretch and shows they can overcome a deficit. For Washington, the night is a reminder that a lopsided shot count counts for little when the goalie at the other end is this sharp.
